plan.topic: Tirzepatide weight-loss plateau: what the randomized trials show about when and why average weight loss levels off (SURMOUNT-1, NEJM 2022: adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes, 72 weeks), the well-documented biology of metabolic adaptation after weight loss, why responses vary between people, and guideline-recommended habits plus questions for your prescriber
plan.angle: Keep the title 'Tirzepatide Weight Loss Plateau: What the Trials Show' and the thumbnail 'Stuck at Month 9?'. Rewrite the first answer in the 0–15 s opening as follows: 'If your weight has stalled, you're not alone. In an analysis of the SURMOUNT-1 trial, most people's weight levelled off at some point, typically somewhere between about 6 and 9 months in. A plateau is an expected part of the curve. It's worth talking through with your prescriber, not a reason to change anything on your own.' In chapter 1, give two separate views and keep them apart: (a) the average NEJM curve, which kept falling for most of the trial and flattened late, from about week 60 (say 'about' and read it from the figure); (b) the individual-plateau post hoc (Chigutsa et al., Clinical Obesity 2025). For (b), say it defined a plateau as 'less than 5% change over 12 weeks', give the median times as roughly 24 to 36 weeks depending on starting BMI, and say that about 9 in 10 had plateaued by week 72. Call it a post hoc analysis by the manufacturer's researchers. Never say 'the trial plateaued at month 9'. In chapter 2, label metabolic adaptation as research mostly from diet-induced weight loss. In chapter 5, add one sentence: 'Don't raise your dose, add supplements or other weight-loss products, or cut calories drastically to break a plateau. Talk to your prescriber.' Keep the rest of the plan as written: the GI line, 'averages, not predictions', 'don't change, stop or switch your medicines on your own', the kidney-disease caveat on protein, 'Not personal advice' and the full prescriber line, the ending with no titles spoken, and no dose or titration numbers anywhere in the narration.

plan.why: Next in the playbook's Lane A queue; long-tail searches like 'mounjaro stopped losing weight' have steady demand. It rests on settled NEJM trial data and peer-reviewed physiology, so it should pass fact-check, and it doesn't overlap today's S1–S3, C1 or the dropped stopping video. | fact-check: Good Lane A topic. It's practical, people search for it, it's evergreen, and it fits the playbook. The science holds up. SURMOUNT-1 (Jastreboff et al., NEJM 2022) had 2,539 adults without diabetes. Weight change at week 72 was −15.0%, −19.5% and −20.9% on 5, 10 and 15 mg, versus −3.1% on placebo, with a 20-week dose-escalation period. The average curves flattened late in the trial, from roughly week 60 onward when read from the figure, not at month 9. The fix: there is a peer-reviewed post hoc analysis that looks directly at individual plateaus. Chigutsa et al., Clinical Obesity 2025, DOI 10.1111/cob.12734, Lilly-funded post hoc of SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-4. It defined a plateau as less than 5% weight change over a 12-week interval and every later 12-week interval. Median time to plateau in SURMOUNT-1 was about 24–36 weeks depending on BMI class (24.3, 26.0, 36.1 and 36.1 weeks). About 88–90% had reached a plateau by week 72. Higher doses, younger participants and women took longer. So the 'month 9' hook is defensible for individuals, but only if this paper is cited and its loose definition is explained. You can't hang it on the average NEJM curve. Main risks: (1) Saying 'the trial levelled off at month 9' would misread the figure. (2) 'Not proof the medicine stopped working' needs balance. A plateau that comes early, or regain, is something to raise with the prescriber, not to self-diagnose. (3) The plateau topic invites self-escalation of dose, extra restriction or adding other weight-loss products. The script must say clearly not to do any of these. (4) The metabolic adaptation research comes mostly from diet-induced weight loss (Rosenbaum & Leibel; Hall's models). Don't claim it has been measured in tirzepatide users unless a source shows that. Other references are fine as planned. The 2025 joint nutrition advisory (Mozaffarian et al., ACLM/ASN/OMA/TOS) exists. SURMOUNT-2 (Garvey et al., Lancet 2023) is the 72-week trial in type 2 diabetes with smaller averages. Use the exact figures from each paper. Keep the plan's chapter structure and the safety lines it lists.

package.description:
Quick answer: In SURMOUNT-1 (adults without diabetes, 72 weeks), the average weight curve flattened late, from about week 60. A manufacturer-funded post hoc analysis of people who lost at least 5% and stayed on treatment found a median of roughly 24–36 weeks to a plateau (under 5% change in 12 weeks), depending on starting BMI. Common side effects were digestive, like nausea.

Not personal advice. Don't change, stop or switch your medicines on your own. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources:
Jastreboff AM et al. NEJM 2022 (SURMOUNT-1) https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2206038
Horn DB et al. Clin Obes 2025 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12096058/
Aronne LJ et al. JAMA 2024 (SURMOUNT-4) https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2023.24945
Polidori D et al. Obesity 2016 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5108589/

script.hook_pattern: Visceral 'you' scenario (the same number on the scale again), then the first answer within 15 seconds, with two open loops: the appetite experiment (paid off in chapter 2) and the trial result that sheds light on 'has the medicine stopped working?' (paid off in chapter 4)

scenes.section: Stuck on the scale?
scenes.narration: You step on the scale. Same number as last week. Same as the week before.

visual.stock_query: frustrated person on bathroom scale morning

scenes.retention_device: Pattern interrupt: a lived moment the viewer recognises

scenes.section: Stuck on the scale?
scenes.narration: If your weight has stalled, you're not alone. A later analysis looked at people on tirzepatide in SURMOUNT one who lost at least five percent and stayed on their treatment. Almost all of them levelled off at some point, typically around six to eight months in.

visual.stat_label: Median time to plateau, tirzepatide, post hoc, people who lost 5%+
visual.stock_query: calendar pages with gentle flat line

scenes.section: Stuck on the scale?
scenes.narration: A plateau is an expected part of the curve. It's worth talking through with your prescriber, not a reason to change anything on your own.

visual.stock_query: calm patient chatting with friendly doctor

scenes.section: Stuck on the scale?
scenes.narration: If part of you has whispered, 'maybe I'm doing this wrong,' that feeling is really common. But the biology says a slowdown isn't simply a willpower problem.

visual.stock_query: worried person at kitchen table night

scenes.retention_device: Name the feeling, then validate it

scenes.section: Stuck on the scale?
scenes.narration: Next: when plateaus show up in the trials, why your body slows the loss, and what actually helps.

scenes.section: Stuck on the scale?
scenes.narration: Plus, one experiment with a diabetes pill that shows how hard your appetite fights back. And the trial result that sheds light on the big question: does a plateau mean the medicine stopped working?

visual.stock_query: curious magnifying glass over question mark

scenes.retention_device: Two open loops: appetite experiment (chapter 2) and 'stopped working?' (chapter 4)

scenes.section: Stuck on the scale?
scenes.narration: Imagine Dana, forty-seven, about nine months into treatment. She's eating well, she feels better, and the scale has barely moved in about three months. Dana is hypothetical, but her question is real.

visual.stock_query: woman looking at scale puzzled hopeful

scenes.retention_device: Relatable thread that runs through the video

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: First, the timing. There are two different ways to look at it, so let's keep them apart.
scenes.retention_device: Chapter change with a clear frame

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: View one is the average curve from SURMOUNT one, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in twenty twenty-two.

visual.stock_query: journal page with falling line graph

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: It enrolled two thousand five hundred thirty-nine adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition. None had diabetes. About three in four got tirzepatide and one in four got placebo, for seventy-two weeks.

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: Counting everyone who started, average weight change at seventy-two weeks was about fifteen percent on the lowest dose and about twenty-one percent on the highest, versus about three percent on placebo.

visual.stock_query: bar chart three bars versus small bar

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: Now look at the shape. The average line kept falling for most of the trial, and only flattened late, from about week sixty, reading it from the figure.

visual.stock_query: line graph curving gently flat near end

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: So on average, the loss didn't stall early. But averages hide individuals.

visual.fact: Read from the figure: it flattened late, around week 60

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: An average blends thousands of people: some still losing, some already steady. So what happens to one person?

visual.stock_query: many cartoon people on different paths

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: That's view two: a post hoc analysis of SURMOUNT one and SURMOUNT four, published in Clinical Obesity in twenty twenty-five by the manufacturer's researchers, and funded by the manufacturer.

visual.stock_query: researcher zooming into one dot on graph

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: Post hoc means the question was asked after the trial, using its data. Useful, but weaker evidence than the trial's main result.

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: They defined a plateau as less than five percent change in weight over twelve weeks, and over every twelve-week stretch after that.

visual.stock_query: twelve week calendar with small arrow

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: Notice how loose that is. Someone still losing slowly, say three percent over three months, would count as plateaued.

visual.stock_query: slow snail still moving forward smiling

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: Using that definition, the median time to a plateau on tirzepatide was roughly twenty-four to thirty-six weeks, depending on starting BMI. In the raw numbers, people with a higher starting BMI tended to plateau later, though that link didn't hold up once other factors were accounted for.

visual.stat_label: Median time to plateau, analysed group, by BMI

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: And by week seventy-two, about nine in ten of the people in that analysis had plateaued by that definition.
scenes.on_screen_text: Most in the analysis levelled off

visual.stat_label: Plateaued by week 72, analysed group, post hoc definition

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: So Dana's three-month stall fits a pattern many people in that analysis went through. It's a normal chapter, not the end of the story.

visual.stock_query: Dana turning page of storybook relieved

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide weight loss level off?
scenes.narration: But why does it happen at all? The answer starts with something your body was doing long before any medicine existed.

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: Let's talk metabolic adaptation. One honest label first: most of this research comes from weight loss through diet, and sometimes exercise, not from people on tirzepatide.

visual.stock_query: body engine with gears and label

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: The simple part: a smaller body needs less energy to run. Less tissue to fuel, less weight to carry up the stairs.

visual.stock_query: cartoon body with smaller fuel tank

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: So the eating pattern that once created a big calorie gap creates a smaller one as you lose. Loss slows, and weight settles at a new level.

visual.stock_query: two bars slowly meeting in middle

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: You may have heard the old rule: cut five hundred calories a day, lose a pound a week, forever. Kevin Hall's team at the National Institutes of Health showed that rule overpredicts long-term loss, because it ignores this slowdown.

visual.myth: 500 fewer calories = 1 lb a week, forever
visual.fact: Loss slows as your body adapts
visual.stock_query: old rulebook with crossed out page

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: Then there's a second layer. Work by Rosenbaum and Leibel at Columbia found that after weight loss, the body often burns even less than its smaller size alone would predict.

visual.stock_query: energy meter reading lower than expected

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: It's called adaptive thermogenesis. Think of it as your body quietly turning down the thermostat to save fuel.

visual.stock_query: body character turning down thermostat dial

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: The most famous example is a small study of fourteen contestants from the TV show The Biggest Loser.

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: Six years later, their resting metabolism was still, on average, about five hundred calories a day lower than expected for their size. That was extreme diet and exercise, not medicine, and only fourteen people.

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: But a slower metabolism alone can't explain how early weight levels off. The bigger force isn't how much you burn. It's how much you want to eat.
scenes.retention_device: 'But here's where it gets weird' re-hook

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: Here's the experiment I promised. Researchers studied people with type 2 diabetes taking canagliflozin, a pill that makes you lose sugar, and its calories, in your urine.

visual.stock_query: pill with sugar cubes floating away

scenes.retention_device: Payoff of the first open loop

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: That calorie loss is steady and measurable, so the team could calculate how much extra people ate to make up for it.

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: The result: for every kilogram lost, appetite rose by about one hundred calories a day.

visual.stat_label: Extra appetite per kg lost, canagliflozin study

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: That's more than three times the slowdown in calories burned. A kilogram is roughly a bag of sugar. Lose five, and your appetite pushes back with about a small meal's worth of calories every day.

visual.stock_query: tug of war appetite versus scale

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: The authors concluded this appetite pushback is a major reason weight loss slows and stalls. Not a character flaw. Biology.

scenes.section: Why does weight loss slow down?
scenes.narration: One caveat: this wasn't measured in people on tirzepatide, and the trials we're covering didn't test how tirzepatide changes this tug-of-war at a plateau.

visual.stock_query: question mark over rope tug of war

scenes.section: Why do some people plateau sooner?
scenes.narration: Now the part that stings most: comparing yourself to someone else. Your friend kept losing for a year. You stalled at month six. Why?

scenes.section: Why do some people plateau sooner?
scenes.narration: First, the trials show a wide spread. In SURMOUNT one, counting everyone who started, about nine in ten on the highest dose lost at least five percent of their weight by week seventy-two, versus about one in three on placebo.

visual.stat_label: Lost 5%+ by week 72: tirzepatide 15 mg vs placebo

scenes.section: Why do some people plateau sooner?
scenes.narration: But only a little over half on that dose lost twenty percent or more. Same medicine, same trial, very different results.

scenes.section: Why do some people plateau sooner?
scenes.narration: The plateau analysis found patterns in timing too. People on higher doses, younger people, and women tended to take longer to plateau.

scenes.section: Why do some people plateau sooner?
scenes.narration: Diabetes matters too. SURMOUNT two enrolled nine hundred thirty-eight adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity, for seventy-two weeks.

scenes.section: Why do some people plateau sooner?
scenes.narration: Counting everyone who started, average weight loss was about thirteen to fifteen percent depending on dose, versus about three percent on placebo.

scenes.section: Why do some people plateau sooner?
scenes.narration: That's smaller than in SURMOUNT one. Separate trials, not head-to-head, but a reminder that results differ between groups of people.

visual.stock_query: two separate trial folders side by side

scenes.section: Why do some people plateau sooner?
scenes.narration: And no trial average can capture your sleep, your stress, your other medicines, or the year you're having.

visual.stock_query: tired parent juggling life at night

scenes.section: Why do some people plateau sooner?
scenes.narration: So here's the key idea: these are averages, not predictions. Your curve is yours.

visual.stock_query: unique fingerprint shaped like a curve

scenes.section: Why do some people plateau sooner?
scenes.narration: Which brings us to what Dana is really asking. If the scale stops, has the medicine stopped working?

scenes.section: Does a plateau mean tirzepatide stopped working?
scenes.narration: Here's the trial result I promised at the start.
scenes.retention_device: Payoff of the main open loop begins

scenes.section: Does a plateau mean tirzepatide stopped working?
scenes.narration: In SURMOUNT four, seven hundred eighty-three adults with obesity or overweight, without diabetes, began thirty-six weeks on tirzepatide.

visual.stock_query: group of adults starting a journey

scenes.section: Does a plateau mean tirzepatide stopped working?
scenes.narration: Then, at week thirty-six, six hundred seventy people on their maximum tolerated dose of ten or fifteen milligrams were randomly split. Three hundred thirty-five kept taking tirzepatide, and three hundred thirty-five were switched to placebo.

scenes.section: Does a plateau mean tirzepatide stopped working?
scenes.narration: Over the next year, the group who stayed on tirzepatide lost about five and a half percent more on average. The placebo group regained about fourteen percent of their body weight.

visual.stock_query: two lines one steady one rising

scenes.section: Does a plateau mean tirzepatide stopped working?
scenes.narration: This trial didn't pick people at a plateau, but it shows that staying on treatment helped hold weight off while the placebo group regained.

scenes.section: Does a plateau mean tirzepatide stopped working?
scenes.narration: So for many people, holding steady isn't nothing. Keeping weight off can be part of what the medicine is doing, even when the scale has slowed.

scenes.section: Does a plateau mean tirzepatide stopped working?
scenes.narration: But here's the honest balance. A plateau that comes very early, or weight that starts creeping back, is worth raising with your prescriber. Don't diagnose it yourself.

visual.stock_query: patient writing note for doctor visit

scenes.section: Does a plateau mean tirzepatide stopped working?
scenes.narration: And don't change, stop or switch your medicines on your own. Those are decisions to make with your prescriber.

scenes.section: Does a plateau mean tirzepatide stopped working?
scenes.narration: Also, the scale isn't the only scoreboard. In SURMOUNT one, waist size, blood pressure and fasting insulin improved on tirzepatide compared with placebo.

scenes.section: Does a plateau mean tirzepatide stopped working?
scenes.narration: So Dana's quiet scale doesn't tell her what her blood pressure, blood sugar or strength are doing. Those are worth asking about.

visual.stock_query: Dana checking blood pressure cuff smiling

scenes.section: Does a plateau mean tirzepatide stopped working?
scenes.narration: So if a plateau is expected, and the medicine may still be helping, what can you actually do? This is the part you can use today.

scenes.section: What helps during a tirzepatide plateau?
scenes.narration: First, what not to do. Don't raise your dose, add supplements or other weight-loss products, or cut calories drastically to break a plateau. Talk to your prescriber.

scenes.section: What helps during a tirzepatide plateau?
scenes.narration: Drastic restriction can leave you short on protein and nutrients, the opposite of what your body needs right now.

visual.stock_query: nearly empty plate with sad vegetables

scenes.section: What helps during a tirzepatide plateau?
scenes.narration: Instead, a twenty twenty-five joint advisory from four nutrition and obesity groups, including the Obesity Society and the American Society for Nutrition, set out priorities for people on GLP-1 medicines.

visual.stock_query: four expert characters around a table

scenes.section: What helps during a tirzepatide plateau?
scenes.narration: One: protein at every meal, to help protect muscle while you lose fat. If you have kidney disease, check your protein target with your clinician first.

visual.stock_query: salmon eggs and beans on plate

scenes.section: What helps during a tirzepatide plateau?
scenes.narration: Two: fiber-rich, minimally processed foods, like vegetables, beans, whole grains and fruit. Fiber also helps with constipation.

visual.stock_query: colorful bowl of vegetables and grains

scenes.section: What helps during a tirzepatide plateau?
scenes.narration: Three: fluids. A smaller appetite can mean drinking less without noticing.

scenes.section: What helps during a tirzepatide plateau?
scenes.narration: On side effects: in SURMOUNT one, the most common on tirzepatide were digestive, like nausea, diarrhea, constipation and vomiting, mostly mild to moderate and most often while the dose was being increased.

visual.stock_query: person holding tummy with ginger tea

scenes.section: What helps during a tirzepatide plateau?
scenes.narration: Four: strength training. The World Health Organization recommends adults do muscle-strengthening activities on two or more days a week, plus one hundred fifty to three hundred minutes of moderate activity.

scenes.section: What helps during a tirzepatide plateau?
scenes.narration: Five: track more than the scale. Your waist, how clothes fit, how easily you climb the stairs. These can show progress the scale misses.

visual.stock_query: tape measure and happy stair climber

scenes.section: What helps during a tirzepatide plateau?
scenes.narration: And bring questions to your prescriber. Is this plateau expected for me? Could another medicine or condition be playing a role? Which health markers should we check? What's our plan from here?

scenes.narration: That last one matters. A plateau plan is made together, not alone at the kitchen counter at ten p.m.

factcheck.summary:
The script is accurate, carefully framed and safe. I checked the post hoc plateau paper (S2, Horn et al., Clin Obes 2025) directly. It confirms the plateau definition (less than 5% change in a 12-week interval and every 12-week interval after it). It also confirms the SURMOUNT-1 median time to plateau by BMI (24.3, 26.0, 36.1 and 36.1 weeks), 87.6–90.2% plateaued by week 72, and later plateaus with higher doses, younger age and female sex. BMI wasn't significant after adjustment.

The other figures match what I know of the published papers, though I didn't reopen those pages this session:
- SURMOUNT-1: about −15% to −21% vs −3.1%, counting everyone who started; 91% vs 35% lost at least 5%; 57% on the highest dose lost 20% or more.
- SURMOUNT-2: 938 adults; about −12.8% to −14.7% vs −3.2%.
- SURMOUNT-4: 783 began the lead-in, 670 were randomized 335/335 at week 36; −5.5% vs +14.0% from week 36 to 88.
- Polidori: about 100 kcal/day of extra appetite per kg lost, more than 3 times the drop in energy burned.
- Fothergill: 14 contestants, about 500 kcal/day below expected.
- Hall 2011 and the WHO 2020 activity guidelines (2 or more strength days; 150–300 minutes of moderate activity).

A web search confirmed that the 2025 joint advisory (ACLM/ASN/OMA/TOS) exists, in Am J Clin Nutr volume 122, pages 344–367. The other sources match their known bibliographic details.

Framing is good: post hoc and manufacturer-funded labels, research from dieting rather than tirzepatide, "separate trials, not head-to-head", the SURMOUNT-4 "didn't pick people at a plateau" limit, Dana clearly labelled as hypothetical, a kidney-disease protein caveat, and the don't stop/switch line plus the prescriber line. Four minor wording fixes are listed below.

issues.claim: Almost all of them levelled off at some point, typically around six to eight months in.
issues.problem: The S2 medians are 24.3–36.1 weeks, which is about 5.5–8.3 months, so 'six to eight months' slightly overstates the low end. The analysed group also had to take at least 75% of doses with no dose reduction. 'Stayed on their treatment' covers this loosely.
issues.fix: s02 narration: "A later analysis looked at people on tirzepatide in SURMOUNT one who lost at least five percent and kept taking their doses. Almost nine in ten levelled off by week seventy-two, typically somewhere around six months to eight months in." s02 stat_value: "About 24–36 weeks". s70: replace "typically around six to eight months in" with "typically around twenty-four to thirty-six weeks in".

issues.claim: published in Clinical Obesity in twenty twenty-five by the manufacturer's researchers, and funded by the manufacturer
issues.problem: The lead author (Horn) is an academic clinician, not a manufacturer employee. Co-authors include Lilly staff. 'By the manufacturer's researchers' misattributes the authorship.
issues.fix: "That's view two: a post hoc analysis of SURMOUNT one and SURMOUNT four, published in Clinical Obesity in twenty twenty-five. Several authors work for the manufacturer, and it was funded by the manufacturer."

issues.claim: The placebo group regained about fourteen percent of their body weight.
issues.problem: SURMOUNT-4 reports +14.0% weight change from randomization (week 36) to week 88. The wording should keep that reference point so it isn't read as 14% of starting weight.
issues.fix: "Over the next year, the group who stayed on tirzepatide lost about five and a half percent more on average, while the placebo group's weight went up by about fourteen percent from where it was at week thirty-six."

issues.problem: This figure is SURMOUNT-1 only (87.6–90.2% by BMI group). The label should name the trial so it isn't read as the combined SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-4 analysis.
issues.fix: stat_label: "Plateaued by week 72, SURMOUNT-1 analysed group, post hoc definition"

thumbnail.reasoning: All three are clean, on-brand (blue/dark/yellow palette, single labelled mascot, no title repetition) and legible at phone size. #1 "9 IN 10" wins on CTR: a concrete, surprising statistic plus the "HIT A PLATEAU" subtitle gives instant context without fully answering the question, the red arrow creates a single strong focal point pointing straight at the scale mascot's shocked expression, and the big-number format reads in under a second even at 168px. #0 ("STUCK AT MONTH 9?") is a close second — strong self-recognition hook — but the 3-line wrap is a touch denser than #1's two clean text blocks. #2 ("WHY IT STALLS") is legible but the headline is the vaguest of the three and doesn't tease a specific number or detail, giving it the weakest curiosity gap. None are misleading relative to the title, which the video (SURMOUNT-1 post hoc plateau data) fully supports.

issues.claim: found most levelled off earlier, typically around 6 to 8 months in
issues.problem: The script doesn't say that most people levelled off before week 60. It says about nine in ten had plateaued by week 72, with a median of roughly 24–36 weeks, and that plateaus came "typically around six to eight months in". A median means half of people, not most. The comment also leaves out the loose definition of a plateau.
issues.fix: But a manufacturer-funded post hoc analysis of people who lost at least 5% and stayed on tirzepatide found plateaus (under 5% change in 12 weeks) typically came around 6 to 8 months in.

issues.claim: found a median of roughly 24-36 weeks to a plateau (under 5% change in 12 weeks)
issues.problem: The script says the range depends on starting BMI. Without that, the range could read as uncertainty around a single number.
issues.fix: A manufacturer-funded post hoc analysis of people who lost at least 5% and stayed on treatment found a median of roughly 24–36 weeks to a plateau (under 5% change in 12 weeks), depending on starting BMI.
